{"summary":"Incremental review of the WP11 shared-IP API-only migration. This is not a whole-WP acceptance. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR defects in the supplied diff.

- **Endpoint coverage:** All 18 non-payment routes now import `checkRateLimit` from the trusted helper. Only the import line changed in each, so the keys, limits and windows stay the same. The same-origin and auth checks and their order relative to the limiter are also unchanged. The route tests cover 23 HTTP handlers with the real resolver and the in-memory limiter. They check that no database or auth work happens before the limiter.
- **Fail-closed behaviour:** When no trusted source is available, the helper returns 503 with `Retry-After: 30`. Forged metadata is rejected: `x-vercel-forwarded-for` is trusted only in the verified Preview-only native mode, and comma-separated lists fail. The trusted address replaces the forwarding headers that the old limiter reads, so rotating forged headers can't create new buckets. The tests check this at the exact threshold for every handler.
- **Body preservation:** The limiter only gets a copy of the request with the method and headers. The route keeps the original request, so its unread body is untouched.
- **New GET live-interactions limit:** It is a separate bucket, `live-interactions-read`, at 120/min. It runs before input validation and database work and doesn't affect the POST limit.

**Deployment note (not a defect in this scope):** This applies to every environment, including local dev and E2E. If `ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_TRUST_MODE` / `ENTRY_CLIENT_IP_DEPLOYMENT_SOURCE` aren't set, all 18 routes return 503. That includes password reset, LINE login, form submissions and CSP reports. Runtime/node mode also only works if the server adapter actually sets `request.ip`. Before this ships, the owned ingress config and the E2E/dev environment setup need to be confirmed.

**Out of scope:** The remaining 8 raw action/helper callers and the commercial Upstash setup were not checked. I can't tell from the supplied text whether those callers share any key strings with these routes. If they do, a spoofable caller could fill up a trusted bucket. Please check this in that separate scope.

The one finding below is about capacity behind shared IPs.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/app/api/live-interactions/route.ts","area":"GET handler, new lines 217-219 (live-interactions-read 120/60_000)","issue":"The viewer polling endpoint had no limit before and now has a per-IP limit of 120/min. It wasn't checked whether that is enough for viewers who share one IP (carrier-grade NAT, venue or office NAT, and the native IPv6 /64 bucket).","evidence":"The diff adds checkRateLimit(request, "live-interactions-read", 120, 60_000) to GET, which had no limiter before. Every viewer behind the same resolved IP shares one bucket. The supplied text gives no client polling interval, no expected number of viewers per IP, and no client handling for 429 or backoff.","impact":"Say the client polls every 2-5 s (12-30 requests/min per viewer). Then about 4-10 viewers behind one shared IP would use up the bucket. After that, real viewers would get 429s and lose live interaction updates during a stream. This is an availability regression on an endpoint that never returned 429 before.","recommended_fix":"Base the 120/min value on the real polling interval times the expected number of viewers per IP. Alternatively, add a second bucket keyed per viewer session alongside a looser IP cap. Also make sure the polling client backs off on 429/503 using Retry-After instead of looping tightly.","required_test":"A client or integration test that confirms the polling interval and that it backs off on 429 and on 503 with Retry-After. A route test showing N simultaneous viewers behind one IP stay under the limit, where N is the documented target.","confidence":0.45}]}
